items.subject: You're Approved to Preregister for FSY 2027!
items.summary: You are approved to preregister for an FSY conference in summer 2027; timing depends on whether your stake is on-cycle.
items.action: Check your stake's FSY cycle and preregister
items.body:
Dear Caiden Lee,

We're excited to invite you to attend a For the Strength of Youth (FSY) conference in summer 2027! FSY is a five-day experience where you'll meet new friends, have fun, feel God's love, and increase your testimony that Jesus Christ is your loving Savior.

You've already received your bishopric's approval to preregister. If your stake is on-cycle this year, you can preregister now. If your stake is off-cycle, you can preregister for FSY beginning on February 15, 2027.

On-cycle preregistration is the first phase of FSY registration. Youth indicate their preferred sessions and can request to be at a session with other participants by using a session link. Session links help participants be at the same session but do not place them in the same room or group.

Your FSY Dashboard is where you can preregister, find session updates, and edit your registration information.

items.subject: Give it everything you've got
items.summary: Sister Heintzelman shares her weekly mission update as her mission nears its end, including a baptism and her homecoming plans.
items.body:
Apparently when you try to avoid talking or thinking about your mission ending, everyone else gets the exact opposite idea. Every member and missionary that I know has been asking me about going home and my last meals. For some strange reason it feels like I'm on death row and they are trying to feed me well before I die.

Speaking of which we had a very busy week. So let's hit the highlights.

A very sweet and tender talk with Hermana Pineda.

Spanish exchange with Sister McDonald in La Joya! We got chased by many dogs, had a cool lesson, and did lots of finding. And the friend we taught, Cesar, got baptized on Sunday!

We had an awesome lesson with Gabriel, Neydy, and two of their kids. We hope that they will get to church soon.

Brenda has been reading her Book of Mormon. There is a lot going on in her life and some opposition, please pray for her.

Hardest point of this week was when our dear friend Maria decided she would no longer come to church or be baptized. I am so grateful to have been part of her story and I know that God is looking out for her and slowly guiding her home.

I want you all to know that God can make the most beautiful garden out of your worst desert. The joy comes in doing the work, not in seeing the results. Trust Him, His plan and timing.

May God be with you all til we meet again.

Sister Heintzelman

Also if you want the information for my arrival and my homecoming, go ahead and reach out!

items.subject: Great and dreadful day pt2
items.summary: Elder Schmidt shares a mission update from Africa about staying in his area, moving apartments, and a devotional on keeping your testimony.
items.body:
Hey everyone hows life going? The work of the Lord is still booming for me down here in Africa.

For now, let's talk about transfers. I am staying in the same area with the same companion, which I am very much not mad about. Here's where things get interesting: I am moving apartments. I was in the celestial apartment, with minimal cockroaches (I only see 5-10 a day) and no mice. My next home is an apartment that the church just bought, so who knows what it's going to be like. I don't have official transfer news yet, so I don't know who my new roommates will be.

Spiritual thought:

On Tuesday we had the opportunity to hear a devotional from Elder Morrison of the 70. He began by talking about testimonies, and how if we are not actively working to grow or protect them the devil will begin to break them. He talked about how when we finish our mission it is important that we continue to keep and build what we gained here. As important as those spiritual experiences are, it's almost more important what happens after.

So when you have a testimony building experience, make sure you continue to maintain and build what you gained, otherwise it will have been for nothing.

Love yall and have a great week!

items.subject: Yup Thats Mamalodi
items.summary: Elder Nelson writes about zone leader exchanges in Mamelodi, eight investigators at church, and a funny lesson on patience.
items.body:
Matthew 10:38, 39. And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me. He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.

This week Wednesday we went on zone leader exchanges. It was priceless to see our beloved zone leader walk through Mamelodi. He did not feel comfortable. We went to a lesson in an informal settlement. When we showed up to meet the guy (Sam), the water turned on. He said it was a miracle and we were sent from God.

This week was an amazing week for sharing the gospel. We had 8 investigators show up to church, one of which was Sam! During Elders Quorum the brother giving the lesson wrote the word patience in big letters on the board and asked us all ways in which we could be patient. Then he asked who all read the conference talk sent on the group chat. Nobody raised their hand. His patience immediately went out the window. Sam our investigator thought it was so funny. He said next week he would bring his family to church.

Going to the zoo with my district!

Love yall,
Elder Nelson

items.subject: Transfer 3!!
items.summary: Elder Andersen shares his transfer news, a new area in Montana, and a baptism commitment from someone he and his companion taught.
items.body:
Wassup gang, so sorry it's been a few weeks since my last email, there was a lot of absolutely nothing going on for a few weeks so I didn't care to write anything. ANYWAYS, transfers happened.

But before I get into that, 2 days before transfers, me and Elder Langston put someone on date! We went to visit her, her name is Sue. During the lesson I thought "invite her to be baptized" and after, Langston had thought the same thing. We went back to Sue's house, Langston shared 2 Nephi 2:2 and she said she was reading that as we knocked on her door. We asked her to be baptized and she said she was just thinking the same thing as we left her house earlier. She accepted the invitation. The spirit was so strong.

Then it was a few busy days until transfers. I got the news I'm going to the west side, to the Bitterroot YSA area! SO PRETTY OVER HERE! My new companion is Elder Welch, who has been out about 18 months. We are the Bitterroot Zone Leaders. We also live with 2 other elders in a trailer house, and Welch and I have been cleaning the place out. I love it here and I love you all!

Thanks to the people who sent me the most elite Halloween packages and snacks! Keep living it up wherever you are.

New address: [removed]
